A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe LoSiA and LoSiA-Pro, including Appendix A on pages 12–18. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical research content. Differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date identification and PDF metadata.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, continual-learning experiments, and resource measurements in Section 4 and Appendices A.2–A.4.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original experimental results, including benchmark scores, robustness analyses, continual-learning outcomes, and training-resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical sensitivity-based subnet localization, greedy selection, asynchronous reselection, learning-rate rewarming, and LoSiA-Pro procedures. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MetaMathQA, Magicoder, and Alpaca-GPT4 training with GSM8K, MBPP, and MMLU evaluation, the same eight commonsense tasks, and the same sequential-learning and masking scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments: Tables 1–2 retain their LoRA, PiSSA, DoRA, and GaLore entries, Table 1 retains its full-fine-tuning references, and Table 5 retains Seq-LoRA.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.3 report identical sampling protocols, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, hyperparameters, and sequential task order. Resource-measurement settings in Appendix A.4 also match.

E4.justification: The same localization, rewarming, and output-layer ablations remain, together with time-slot/data-scale sensitivity, rank-factor robustness, masking tests, neuron-selection analyses, and singular-vector comparisons in Section 4 and the appendix.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3.1 retains the statement that all experiments use a single run. Run-count disclosure, seed information, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains LoSiA's 70.35 average accuracy, Table 5 retains Seq-LoSiA's 70.48 AP and −3.54 BWT, and Table 15 retains LoSiA-Pro's 244.8 microseconds/token with gradient checkpointing.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.1 retain identical definitions, equations, approximation derivations, and the subnet-selection NP-hardness proof. The memory expressions in Appendix A.4.1 are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about efficient high-rank subnet adaptation, competitive task performance, faster training, and reduced forgetting. No contribution or claim changes in scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning knowledge retention, generalization, training stability, and intruder dimensions are identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning untested applications, rigid subnet localization, multi-GPU support, and time-slot selection.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameter tables, hardware/software disclosures, and resource measurements remain identical. The source-code link and other technical access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to low-rank adaptation, pruning, and skill localization is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 6 Jul 2025 to v3 dated 20 Aug 2025, and PDF author-metadata punctuation is corrected. Body wording, headings, and main-text/appendix organization are identical.

P2.justification: All 12 figures and 15 tables retain identical displays, captions, styling, and placement. Rendered pages match exactly outside the first-page version/date stamp; no figure, table, or page-layout revision occurs.

improvement.justification: The research content, empirical evidence, proofs, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical throughout both PDFs, including their appendices. The administrative version/date and metadata updates produce no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
